````tsx
import { useParams, Link } from 'react-router-dom';
import { Clock, ArrowLeft } from 'lucide-react';
import { SEO } from '../../components/SEO';
import { Breadcrumbs } from '../../components/Breadcrumbs';
import { QuickAnswer, FactsTable, SourcesBox, AuthorBox, RelatedPages } from '../../components/Article';
import { FAQSection } from '../../components/FAQSection';
import { getRegion, computeRegionTimes, REGIONS, type RegionTimes } from '../../lib/regions';
import { getRegionContent } from '../../lib/region-content';
import { articleSchema } from '../../lib/schema';
import { getAuthorName, SITE_CONFIG } from '../../config/site';

const LAST_UPDATED = '2026-11-05';
const LAST_UPDATED_LABEL = 'November 5, 2026';

/**
 * One region's release-time page (Batch 4: full page, not a stub).
 *
 * Times are computed at build time from the verified reference timestamps
 * with Intl.DateTimeFormat — PS5 pre-load is midnight local time, Xbox
 * pre-load is 00:00 GMT, unlock is midnight local time on November 19,
 * 2026. The region-specific editorial copy (intro, launch-day section,
 * pre-load note, editions note, FAQ answers) comes from
 * src/data/region-content.json via src/lib/region-content.ts — one entry
 * per region, each written as genuinely different copy (>=350 unique
 * words per page, gated by `npm run verify:regions`).
 *
 * If a region has no content entry yet, the page falls back to the old
 * generic stub WITH noindex, so nothing thin ships — and verify:regions
 * fails the build, which is the correct outcome.
 */
export function ReleaseTimeRegionPage() {
  const { slug } = useParams<{ slug: string }>();
  const region = getRegion(slug ?? '');

  if (!region) {
    return (
      <>
        <SEO title="Region not found" description="This release-time region does not exist." canonical="/gta-6-release-time" noindex />
        <div className="max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4 py-20 text-center">
          <Clock className="w-16 h-16 text-[#FF2E93]/40 mx-auto mb-4" />
          <h1 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-2xl text-white">Region not found</h1>
          <p className="text-sm text-[#B9A6D4] mt-2 mb-6">
            This region is not in the release-time list yet.
          </p>
          <Link to="/gta-6-release-time" className="inline-flex items-center gap-2 text-sm text-[#19E3D0] hover:underline">
            <ArrowLeft className="w-4 h-4" /> All regions
          </Link>
        </div>
      </>
    );
  }

  const times = computeRegionTimes(region.timezone);
  const content = getRegionContent(region.slug);

  if (!content) {
    return <RegionStubPage region={region} times={times} />;
  }

  // Short names keep the <title> under 60 chars for the long zone names
  // ("GTA 6 Release Time in United States (Eastern) | VICE TOOLS" would be
  // 60 chars; "GTA 6 Release Time in US Eastern | VICE TOOLS" is 46).
  const titleName = content.titleName ?? region.location;
  const seoTitle = `GTA 6 Release Time in ${titleName}`;
  const seoDescription = `When does GTA 6 unlock in ${region.location}? Midnight local time, November 19, 2026. Pre-load from November 10 on PS5 and Xbox.`;
  const canonical = `/gta-6-release-time/${region.slug}`;

  const regionIndex = REGIONS.findIndex((r) => r.slug === region.slug);
  const prevRegion = REGIONS[(regionIndex - 1 + REGIONS.length) % REGIONS.length];
  const nextRegion = REGIONS[(regionIndex + 1) % REGIONS.length];

  return (
    <>
      <SEO
        title={seoTitle}
        description={seoDescription}
        canonical={canonical}
        type="article"
        articlePublished={LAST_UPDATED}
        articleModified={LAST_UPDATED}
        ogImage="https://vicetools.app/og-release.png"
        schema={articleSchema({
          headline: seoTitle,
          description: seoDescription,
          datePublished: LAST_UPDATED,
          dateModified: LAST_UPDATED,
          authorName: getAuthorName(),
          url: `${SITE_CONFIG.url}${canonical}`,
        })}
      />

      <div className="max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8 py-10">
        <Breadcrumbs pathname={canonical} />

        <div className="mt-6">
          <div className="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-3 py-1 rounded-full bg-[#150A24] border border-[#19E3D0]/40 text-xs font-mono text-[#19E3D0] mb-3">
            <Clock className="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
            <span>{region.timezone}</span>
          </div>
          <h1 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-black text-3xl sm:text-4xl text-white leading-tight">
            GTA 6 Release Time in {region.location}
          </h1>
          <p className="text-xs text-[#B9A6D4] font-mono mt-2">Last updated: {LAST_UPDATED_LABEL}</p>
        </div>

        <QuickAnswer>
          GTA 6 unlocks in {region.location} at midnight local time on November 19, 2026 —{' '}
          {times.unlock}. Pre-loading starts November 10, 2026 (PS5 at midnight local, Xbox at
          12:00 AM GMT). The pre-load file is up to 212 GB.
        </QuickAnswer>

        {/* Region-specific intro — inside data-region-content so the
            uniqueness gate counts it. Blocks contain <p>/<strong> only,
            no nested <div>, so the gate regex matches them exactly. */}
        <div data-region-content="true" className="space-y-4 my-6 text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed">
          {content.intro.map((paragraph, i) => (
            <p key={i}>{paragraph}</p>
          ))}
        </div>

        {/* Local-time table (computed, shared template — not gated content) */}
        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl text-white mt-10 mb-3">
          Local times in {region.location}
        </h2>
        <div className="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-2xl border border-white/10">
          <table className="w-full text-sm">
            <thead>
              <tr className="bg-[#150A24] text-left text-xs font-mono uppercase tracking-wider text-[#B9A6D4]">
                <th className="px-4 py-3">Event</th>
                <th className="px-4 py-3">Local time in {region.location}</th>
                <th className="px-4 py-3">Platform</th>
              </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
              <tr className="border-t border-white/5">
                <td className="px-4 py-3 text-white/90">Pre-load begins</td>
                <td className="px-4 py-3 text-white font-mono">{times.ps5Preload}</td>
                <td className="px-4 py-3 text-[#B9A6D4]">PlayStation 5 — midnight local time</td>
              </tr>
              <tr className="border-t border-white/5">
                <td className="px-4 py-3 text-white/90">Pre-load begins</td>
                <td className="px-4 py-3 text-white font-mono">{times.xboxPreload}</td>
                <td className="px-4 py-3 text-[#B9A6D4]">Xbox Series X|S — 12:00 AM GMT</td>
              </tr>
              <tr className="border-t border-white/5">
                <td className="px-4 py-3 text-white/90">Game unlocks</td>
                <td className="px-4 py-3 text-white font-mono">{times.unlock}</td>
                <td className="px-4 py-3 text-[#B9A6D4]">Both consoles — midnight local time</td>
              </tr>
              <tr className="border-t border-white/5">
                <td className="px-4 py-3 text-white/90">Boxed Standard Edition in shops</td>
                <td className="px-4 py-3 text-white font-mono">November 12, 2026</td>
                <td className="px-4 py-3 text-[#B9A6D4]">Code-in-box, no disc</td>
              </tr>
            </tbody>
          </table>
        </div>

        <p className="text-sm text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed mb-6">
          Rockstar has not published a single global unlock hour, and no official
          hour-by-hour unlock map exists. The unlock is local midnight in each
          region — the table above is the local time for {region.location}, computed
          from the verified references, not a conversion of one worldwide instant.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl text-white mt-10 mb-3">
          Launch day in {region.location}
        </h2>
        <div data-region-content="true" className="space-y-4 my-6 text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed">
          <p>{content.launchDay}</p>
        </div>

        <FactsTable
          rows={[
            {
              fact: 'GTA 6 launches November 19, 2026, on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S',
              status: 'confirmed',
              sourceUrl: 'https://www.rockstargames.com/newswire/article/ak3ak31a49a221/grand-theft-auto-vi-is-now-set-to-launch-november-19-2026',
              sourceName: 'Rockstar Newswire',
            },
            {
              fact: 'Pre-load begins November 10, 2026; pre-load file up to 212 GB',
              status: 'confirmed',
              sourceUrl: 'https://www.rockstargames.com/newswire',
              sourceName: 'Rockstar Newswire (Nov 3, 2026)',
            },
            {
              fact: 'The game unlocks at midnight local time on November 19, 2026, in all regions',
              status: 'confirmed',
              sourceUrl: 'https://support.rockstargames.com/',
              sourceName: 'Rockstar Support',
            },
            {
              fact: 'An official hour-by-hour global unlock map from Rockstar',
              status: 'unconfirmed',
            },
          ]}
        />

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl text-white mt-10 mb-3">
          Pre-load in {region.location}
        </h2>
        <div data-region-content="true" className="p-5 rounded-2xl border border-[#FFC857]/30 bg-[#FFC857]/5 text-sm text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed mb-6">
          <p><strong className="text-white">Pre-load note: </strong>{content.preloadNote}</p>
        </div>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl text-white mt-10 mb-3">
          Editions in {region.location}
        </h2>
        <div data-region-content="true" className="space-y-4 my-6 text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed">
          <p>{content.editionsNote}</p>
        </div>

        <FAQSection items={content.faq} title={`GTA 6 in ${region.location} — Questions`} subtitle="" badge="" badgeColor="#FFC857" />

        <SourcesBox
          sources={[
            { name: 'Rockstar Newswire — GTA VI launches November 19, 2026', url: 'https://www.rockstargames.com/newswire/article/ak3ak31a49a221/grand-theft-auto-vi-is-now-set-to-launch-november-19-2026' },
            { name: 'Rockstar Newswire — Pre-load begins November 10, 2026', url: 'https://www.rockstargames.com/newswire' },
            { name: 'Rockstar Support — pre-load guidance', url: 'https://support.rockstargames.com/' },
          ]}
          lastVerified={LAST_UPDATED}
        />

        <AuthorBox />

        <RelatedPages
          pages={[
            { name: 'All regions', path: '/gta-6-release-time' },
            { name: 'GTA 6 release date', path: '/gta-6-release-date' },
            { name: 'GTA 6 pre-load', path: '/gta-6-preload' },
            { name: `Release time in ${prevRegion.location}`, path: `/gta-6-release-time/${prevRegion.slug}` },
            { name: `Release time in ${nextRegion.location}`, path: `/gta-6-release-time/${nextRegion.slug}` },
          ]}
        />
      </div>
    </>
  );
}

/**

function RegionStubPage({ region, times }: { region: { slug: string; location: string; timezone: string }; times: RegionTimes }) {

There is no single global unlock instant; Rockstar has said the game unlocks at local midnight in all regions, on both PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.`,

        <div className="my-6 overflow-x-auto rounded-2xl border border-white/10">
          <table className="w-full text-sm">

              </tr>

            <tbody>
              <tr className="border-t border-white/5">

                <td className="px-4 py-3 text-[#B9A6D4]">PlayStation 5 — midnight local time</td>
              </tr>
              <tr className="border-t border-white/5">

              </tr>
              <tr className="border-t border-white/5">

                <td className="px-4 py-3 text-[#B9A6D4]">Both consoles — midnight local time</td>

import { Link } from 'react-router-dom';
import { MonitorX } from 'lucide-react';
import { SEO } from '../../components/SEO';
import { Breadcrumbs } from '../../components/Breadcrumbs';
import { QuickAnswer, FactsTable, SourcesBox, AuthorBox, RelatedPages } from '../../components/Article';
import { FAQSection } from '../../components/FAQSection';
import { articleSchema } from '../../lib/schema';
import { getAuthorName, SITE_CONFIG } from '../../config/site';

/**
 * Why GTA 6 is not on PC. The honest answer is that Rockstar has not
 * said why and has not announced a PC version at all. The console-first
 * pattern is presented as history — never as a reason Rockstar stated.
 */
export function WhyNoPcPage() {
  const description =
    'Why is GTA 6 not on PC? Rockstar has not announced a PC version or given a reason. The console-first pattern and what Take-Two has said.';
  const url = `${SITE_CONFIG.url}/gta-6-why-no-pc`;

  const faq = [
    {
      question: 'Why is GTA 6 not on PC?',
      answer: 'Rockstar has not given a reason, and has not announced a PC version at all. The studio has a history of launching on console first and bringing games to PC later, but that is a pattern from its past releases — not a reason Rockstar has stated for this game.',
    },
    {
      question: 'Will GTA 6 ever come to PC?',
      answer: 'It has been reported, not confirmed. GamesBeat reported on October 13, 2026 that a PC version is planned for the first quarter of 2027, citing four anonymous industry sources. Rockstar has not confirmed it, and no PC version has been announced.',
    },
    {
      question: 'Did Rockstar say PC players have to wait?',
      answer: 'Rockstar has said nothing about PC at all — no version, no date, no reason. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has said the game has been announced for console only so far. That is the full extent of what the companies have said.',
    },
    {
      question: 'Is it because consoles are more profitable?',
      answer: 'That is speculation, not something Rockstar or Take-Two has said. Console launches concentrate sales into one date, and a later PC launch can sell the game twice — but no executive has given that as the reason for GTA 6, so this page does not present it as one.',
    },
    {
      question: 'Can I play GTA 6 on PC another way at launch?',
      answer: 'No. There is no PC version, no cloud streaming version, and no legitimate PC download. The Xbox Store listing does not show GTA 6 as a Cloud Gaming or Play Anywhere title. Any site offering a PC download before a PC version is announced is a scam.',
    },
  ];

  return (
    <>
      <SEO
        title="Why Is GTA 6 Not on PC? The Real Answer"
        description={description}
        canonical="/gta-6-why-no-pc"
        type="article"
        articlePublished="2026-11-05"
        articleModified="2026-11-05"
        ogImage="https://vicetools.app/og-release.png"
        schema={articleSchema({
          headline: 'Why Is GTA 6 Not on PC? The Real Answer',
          description,
          datePublished: '2026-11-05',
          dateModified: '2026-11-05',
          authorName: getAuthorName(),
          url,
        })}
      />

      <div className="max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8 py-10">
        <Breadcrumbs pathname="/gta-6-why-no-pc" />

        <div className="mt-6">
          <div className="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-3 py-1 rounded-full bg-[#150A24] border border-[#19E3D0]/40 text-xs font-mono text-[#19E3D0] mb-3">
            <MonitorX className="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
            <span>NO PC VERSION ANNOUNCED</span>
          </div>
          <h1 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-black text-3xl sm:text-4xl text-white leading-tight">
            Why Is GTA 6 Not on PC?
          </h1>
          <p className="text-xs font-mono text-[#B9A6D4] mt-3">Last updated: November 5, 2026</p>
        </div>

        <QuickAnswer>
          Rockstar has not announced a PC version of GTA 6, and it has not given a reason for
          that. The game launches November 19, 2026, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only.
          The studio has launched on console first before — GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 both
          reached PC later — but that history is a pattern, not a reason Rockstar has stated.
        </QuickAnswer>

        <FactsTable
          rows={[
            {
              fact: 'No PC version of GTA 6 has been announced — no date, no store page, no system requirements',
              status: 'confirmed',
              sourceUrl: 'https://www.rockstargames.com/VI',
              sourceName: 'Rockstar Games',
            },
            {
              fact: 'GTA 6 launches November 19, 2026, on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S only',
              status: 'confirmed',
              sourceUrl: 'https://www.rockstargames.com/newswire/article/ak3ak31a49a221/grand-theft-auto-vi-is-now-set-to-launch-november-19-2026',
              sourceName: 'Rockstar Newswire',
            },
            {
              fact: 'GamesBeat (Oct 13, 2026): PC version planned for Q1 2027, per four anonymous industry sources; Rockstar did not respond',
              status: 'reported',
              sourceName: 'GamesBeat (Oct 13, 2026)',
            },
            {
              fact: 'A reason given by Rockstar for not announcing a PC version',
              status: 'unconfirmed',
            },
            {
              fact: 'Official GTA 6 PC system requirements',
              status: 'unconfirmed',
            },
          ]}
        />

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          The honest answer: Rockstar has not said
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          There is no official reason for GTA 6 not being on PC, because there is no official
          PC version to give a reason about. Rockstar has not announced a PC version, has not
          dated one, has not shown a store page for one, and has not published system
          requirements for one. Its communications — the Newswire posts, the trailers, the
          editions page, the official GTA VI page — mention only PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series
          X|S. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has said the game has been announced for console
          only so far, and Take-Two&rsquo;s published line-up tables list GTA 6 for PS5 and Xbox
          Series X|S with no PC entry. That is everything the companies have said. Any article
          that tells you the reason — that it is about sales, or piracy, or development
          priorities, or any other cause — is guessing, however confident it sounds.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          The console-first pattern
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          What Rockstar has done before is well documented, and it is the reason most people
          expect a PC version eventually. Grand Theft Auto V launched on consoles in September
          2013 and reached PC about a year and a half later, in April 2015. Red Dead Redemption
          2 launched on consoles in October 2018 and reached PC about a year later, in November
          2019. In both cases the console launch came first, the PC version followed, and the
          PC version arrived with improvements. That pattern is real history — but it is a
          pattern, not a reason. It tells you what Rockstar has done before, not why it is doing
          the same thing now, and it tells you nothing about the date. A first quarter 2027 PC
          window, as GamesBeat reported, would be faster than Rockstar&rsquo;s usual pace — roughly
          two to four months after the console launch instead of a year or more. That is one
          more reason to treat the reported window as a report, not a date.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          What people guess — and why it stays a guess
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          The common guesses are easy to list: a console launch concentrates sales and attention
          into a single date; a later PC launch can sell the same game a second time; building
          for two fixed consoles is simpler than building for the endless variety of PC
          hardware; and a staggered launch spreads the work of supporting the game. Some of
          these are probably true in general. None of them has been stated by Rockstar or
          Take-Two about GTA 6, so none of them belongs on this page as an answer. The same
          applies to the more dramatic theories — that the PC version is being held back for a
          bigger reveal, or that it depends on something else entirely. Until Rockstar speaks,
          the only honest answer to &lsquo;why is GTA 6 not on PC?&rsquo; is &lsquo;Rockstar has not said, and
          has not announced a PC version at all.&rsquo;
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          What PC players should — and should not — do
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          Do not buy anything. There is no PC version to pre-order, no PC key to buy, and no PC
          download — any site selling you one is a scam, and our{' '}
          <Link to="/gta-6-download" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">download safety page</Link> lists
          the tricks to watch for. Do not trust system requirements lists either: none exist,
          and every list online today is invented. Do watch the official sources — the Rockstar
          Newswire and rockstargames.com/VI — because a PC announcement, when it comes, will
          appear there first. And do not assume the console launch tells you anything about the
          PC date: GTA 5&rsquo;s PC version came a year and a half after consoles, Red Dead
          Redemption 2&rsquo;s a year after, and the reported Q1 2027 window would be faster than
          both. The full state of play, including the GamesBeat report in detail, is on our{' '}
          <Link to="/gta-6-pc-release-date" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">GTA 6 PC release date page</Link>.
        </p>

        <FAQSection items={faq} title="Why GTA 6 is not on PC — Questions" subtitle="" badge="" badgeColor="#FFC857" />

        <SourcesBox
          sources={[
            { name: 'Rockstar Games — official GTA VI page (PS5 and Xbox Series X|S only)', url: 'https://www.rockstargames.com/VI' },
            { name: 'Rockstar Newswire — GTA VI is now set to launch November 19, 2026 (Nov 6, 2025)', url: 'https://www.rockstargames.com/newswire/article/ak3ak31a49a221/grand-theft-auto-vi-is-now-set-to-launch-november-19-2026' },
          ]}
          lastVerified="2026-11-05"
        />

        <AuthorBox />

        <RelatedPages
          pages={[
            { name: 'GTA 6 PC release date', path: '/gta-6-pc-release-date' },
            { name: 'GTA 6 platforms', path: '/gta-6-platforms' },
            { name: 'GTA 6 release date', path: '/gta-6-release-date' },
            { name: 'GTA 6 download — official ways & scams', path: '/gta-6-download' },
            { name: 'GTA 6 delay history', path: '/gta-6-delay-history' },
          ]}
        />
      </div>
    </>
  );
}

import { Link } from 'react-router-dom';
import { Mail, MessageSquare, ShieldCheck, ExternalLink } from 'lucide-react';
import { SEO } from '../../components/SEO';
import { Breadcrumbs } from '../../components/Breadcrumbs';
import { getContactEmail } from '../../config/site';

/**
 * Contact page — honest mailto route only. There is no contact form and no
 * backend: the previous version showed a form that claimed a message had
 * been "dispatched" to moderators, but nothing was ever sent anywhere.
 * This version links to the configured contact email with a prefilled
 * subject, and says plainly what happens: your own email app opens and
 * you send the message yourself. If no contact email is configured, the
 * page says the contact email is not set yet instead of showing a fake
 * address.
 */
export function ContactPage() {
  const contactEmail = getContactEmail();
  const mailto = contactEmail
    ? `mailto:${contactEmail}?subject=${encodeURIComponent('VICE TOOLS — Feedback / Suggestion')}`
    : '';

  return (
    <>
      <SEO
        title="Contact VICE TOOLS"
        description="Contact VICE TOOLS by email: corrections, feedback, and suggestions about the GTA 6 companion site."
        canonical="/contact"
      />

      <div className="max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8 py-10">
        <Breadcrumbs pathname="/contact" />

        <div className="mt-6">
          <div className="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-3 py-1 rounded-full bg-[#150A24] border border-[#19E3D0]/40 text-xs font-mono text-[#19E3D0] mb-3">
            <Mail className="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
            <span>EMAIL ONLY • NO FORM • NO BACKEND</span>
          </div>
          <h1 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-black text-3xl sm:text-4xl text-white leading-tight">
            Contact
          </h1>
          <p className="text-xs font-mono text-[#B9A6D4] mt-3">Last updated: November 5, 2026</p>
        </div>

        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-6 font-light">
          We would like to hear from you — especially if you have spotted a factual error, a
          broken link, or a claim that needs a better source. There is no contact form on this
          site: nothing you type here is sent to a server, because there is no server to send
          it to. Instead, use the email link below. It opens your own email app with the
          subject already filled in, and you send the message yourself.
        </p>

        {contactEmail ? (
          <div className="p-6 rounded-xl bg-[#150A24] border border-white/10 my-6">
            <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
              <Mail className="w-5 h-5 text-[#19E3D0] shrink-0" />
              <div>
                <p className="text-sm text-[#B9A6D4]">Email us at</p>
                <a
                  href={mailto}
                  className="text-lg font-bold text-white hover:text-[#19E3D0] break-all"
                >
                  {contactEmail}
                </a>
              </div>
            </div>
            <a
              href={mailto}
              className="mt-5 inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-5 py-3 rounded-lg bg-[#19E3D0] text-[#0B0614] font-bold text-sm hover:bg-white transition-colors"
            >
              <Mail className="w-4 h-4" />
              Open your email app
              <ExternalLink className="w-4 h-4" />
            </a>
            <p className="text-xs text-[#B9A6D4] mt-4">
              The subject line is prefilled as &ldquo;VICE TOOLS — Feedback / Suggestion&rdquo;.
              Your email address and message are used only to reply to you — they are not added
              to any mailing list or shared with anyone. See the{' '}
              <Link to="/privacy" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">
                Privacy Policy
              </Link>{' '}
              for details.
            </p>
          </div>
        ) : (
          <div className="p-6 rounded-xl bg-[#150A24] border border-[#FFC857]/40 my-6">
            <div className="flex items-start gap-3">
              <MessageSquare className="w-5 h-5 text-[#FFC857] shrink-0 mt-0.5" />
              <div>
                <p className="font-bold text-white">Contact email not set yet</p>
                <p className="text-sm text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed mt-2 font-light">
                  The site operator has not set a contact email yet, so there is no email address
                  to show here. This page will list the real address once it is configured. In the
                  meantime, please check the{' '}
                  <Link to="/about/methodology" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">
                    methodology page
                  </Link>{' '}
                  for how facts on this site are verified and corrected.
                </p>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>
        )}

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          What to include in your message
        </h2>
        <ul className="list-disc pl-6 space-y-2 text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed font-light">
          <li>
            <strong className="text-white">For a correction:</strong> the page, the claim, and
            the source that contradicts it (an official Rockstar, PlayStation, or Xbox link if
            you have one). Corrections are checked against the official sources before anything
            changes.

          <li>
            <strong className="text-white">For a broken link or a bug:</strong> the page you
            were on and what happened.

}

export function PrivacyPage() {

  return (
    <>
      <SEO
        title="Privacy Policy"
        description="How VICE TOOLS handles your data: analytics only after your consent, ads off by default, and what is stored in your browser."
        canonical="/privacy"
      />

      <div className="max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8 py-10">
        <Breadcrumbs pathname="/privacy" />

        <h1 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-black text-3xl sm:text-4xl text-white leading-tight mt-6">
          Privacy Policy
        </h1>
        <p className="text-xs font-mono text-[#B9A6D4] mt-3">Last updated: November 5, 2026</p>

        <div className="max-w-none mt-8 space-y-8 text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed font-light">
          <section>
            <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-lg text-white mb-3">
              1. What this site is
            </h2>
            <p>
              VICE TOOLS is an unofficial, fan-made companion site for Grand Theft Auto VI. It is
              not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Rockstar Games or Take-Two
              Interactive. This policy describes what data the site collects, what it stores in
              your browser, and what it does not do.
            </p>
          </section>

          <section>
            <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-lg text-white mb-3">
              2. Analytics — only after your consent
            </h2>
            <p>
              This site can use Google Analytics 4, but only after you consent, and only if an
              analytics ID has been configured by the site operator. Analytics is off by default:
              no analytics script is loaded, and no analytics data is sent, until you accept
              analytics in the cookie banner. If no analytics ID is configured, nothing is sent
              at all — the analytics code is a no-op. When analytics is active and you have
              consented, Google Analytics collects aggregate, anonymised usage data (such as
              which pages are visited) under Google&rsquo;s own privacy terms. You can withdraw
              consent at any time by clearing your cookie choice in your browser and revisiting
              the site, or by using your browser&rsquo;s tracking controls.
            </p>
          </section>

          <section>
            <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-lg text-white mb-3">
              3. Advertising — off by default
            </h2>
            <p>
              Advertising is off by default on this site. No ad slots are rendered and no ad
              scripts are loaded unless the site operator has explicitly enabled advertising, and
              even then only after you have consented to it in the cookie banner. When
              advertising is enabled and you have consented, Google AdSense may set cookies to
              serve and measure ads, under Google&rsquo;s own privacy terms. If you do not
              consent, no ad content is loaded. This site does not sell your data, and it does
              not share personal data with advertisers directly.
            </p>
          </section>

          <section>
            <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-lg text-white mb-3">
              4. Cookies and local storage
            </h2>
            <p>
              The site stores a small amount of data in your own browser, and only there — it is
              never sent to a server by this site:
            </p>
            <ul className="list-disc pl-6 space-y-2 mt-3">
              <li>
                <strong className="text-white">Your cookie choice</strong> — whether you accepted
                or declined analytics and advertising, so the banner does not ask you again on
                every visit.
              </li>
              <li>
                <strong className="text-white">Calculator preferences</strong> — the presets and
                settings you save in the money and loadout calculators, so they are still there
                when you come back.
              </li>
              <li>
                <strong className="text-white">Map preferences</strong> — the markers you have
                found on the interactive map, so your progress is kept.
              </li>
            </ul>
            <p className="mt-3">
              You can delete all of this at any time by clearing your browser&rsquo;s local
              storage and cookies for this site. The site has no account system, no sign-in, and
              no server-side user profiles, so there is nothing to delete on our side.
            </p>
          </section>

          <section>
            <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-lg text-white mb-3">
              5. Contact
            </h2>
            <p>
              If you contact us by email, your email address and message are used only to reply
              to you. They are not added to any mailing list, shared with third parties, or used
              for marketing. There is no contact form on this site that sends data to a server —
              the contact page links to an email address, and your email is sent by your own
              email app.
            </p>
            {contactEmail && (
              <p className="mt-3">
                Contact email:{' '}
                <a href={`mailto:${contactEmail}`} className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">
                  {contactEmail}
                </a>
              </p>
            )}
          </section>

          <section>
            <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-lg text-white mb-3">
              6. Changes to this policy
            </h2>
            <p>
              If this policy changes — for example, if analytics or advertising is enabled — the
              last-updated date at the top of this page changes, and the cookie banner will ask
              for your consent again where required. The version of this policy that applies to
              you is the one published on this page at the time of your visit.
            </p>
          </section>
        </div>
      </div>
    </>
  );
}

import { getAuthorName, SITE_CONFIG } from '../../config/site';

/**
 * Hub 3 spoke — Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. The "why is Lucia in jail"
 * question is answered ONLY with what the official trailers show (she is
 * in prison at the story's start) plus the documented background, and the
 * page states explicitly that Rockstar has not detailed the charges or
 * the backstory. No invented backstory, no invented dialogue.
 */
export function CharactersPage() {
  const description =
    "Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos are GTA 6's two protagonists. What the trailers show, who the supporting cast is, and why Lucia starts the story in prison.";
  const url = `${SITE_CONFIG.url}/gta-6-characters-jason-lucia`;

  const faq = [
    {
      question: 'Who are the main characters in GTA 6?',
      answer: 'Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. They are the two protagonists of GTA 6\u2019s single-player story, and the game is built around their relationship — a duo inspired by Bonnie and Clyde, according to the documented coverage of the game. Both are playable.',
    },
    {
      question: 'Why is Lucia in jail at the start of GTA 6?',
      answer: 'The official trailers show Lucia in prison at the start of the story, and the documented background is that she was imprisoned at Leonida Penitentiary after fighting for her family from Liberty City. Rockstar has not detailed the charges against her, the crime, or the backstory in any official release — so this page does not invent one. What is confirmed is that she is released, reunites with Jason, and the story follows from there.',
    },
    {
      question: 'Is Lucia the first female protagonist in GTA?',
      answer: 'She is the series\u2019 first non-optional female protagonist. Earlier Grand Theft Auto games had female characters you could play in multiplayer or in side content, but Lucia is the first woman to lead a mainline story — and she shares that lead with Jason, rather than carrying it alone.',
    },
    {
      question: 'Who is Jason Duval?',
      answer: 'Jason is one of the two protagonists. The documented background is that he worked for local drug runners in the Leonida Keys after serving in the Army. Trailer 2 shows him living a quiet life in the Keys — fixing roofs, working odd jobs — before Lucia\u2019s release pulls him back into crime.',
    },
    {
      question: 'Can you switch between Jason and Lucia?',
      answer: 'The documented coverage says the two protagonists are switchable, in the style of GTA V\u2019s three-character system. Rockstar has not published a detailed description of how switching works in GTA 6, so the mechanics are reported, not confirmed.',
    },
    {
      question: 'Who else is in GTA 6?',
      answer: 'Supporting characters named in official material include Cal Hampton, Boobie Ike, Dre\u2019Quan Priest, Bae-Luxe and Roxy (the duo Real Dimez), Raul Bautista, and Brian Heder. Their roles are documented from official material; detailed backstories for them have not been published.',
    },
  ];

  return (
    <>
      <SEO
        title="GTA 6 Characters — Jason & Lucia"
        description={description}
        canonical="/gta-6-characters-jason-lucia"
        type="article"
        articlePublished="2026-11-05"
        articleModified="2026-11-05"
        ogImage="https://vicetools.app/og-map.png"
        schema={articleSchema({
          headline: 'GTA 6 Characters — Jason & Lucia',
          description,
          datePublished: '2026-11-05',
          dateModified: '2026-11-05',
          authorName: getAuthorName(),
          url,
        })}
      />

      <div className="max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8 py-10">
        <Breadcrumbs pathname="/gta-6-characters-jason-lucia" />

        <div className="mt-6">
          <div className="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-3 py-1 rounded-full bg-[#150A24] border border-[#19E3D0]/40 text-xs font-mono text-[#19E3D0] mb-3">
            <Users className="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
            <span>DUAL PROTAGONISTS • SINGLE-PLAYER STORY</span>
          </div>
          <h1 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-black text-3xl sm:text-4xl text-white leading-tight">
            Jason &amp; Lucia
          </h1>
          <p className="text-xs font-mono text-[#B9A6D4] mt-3">Last updated: November 5, 2026</p>
        </div>

        <QuickAnswer>
          GTA 6 stars two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, in a single-player
          story set in Vice City and the state of Leonida. Lucia starts the story in prison;
          Jason is trying to stay out of trouble in the Leonida Keys. After a failed bank
          heist, the two of them are drawn into a conspiracy that spans the state.
        </QuickAnswer>

        <FactsTable
          rows={[
            {
              fact: 'The protagonists are Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos',
              status: 'confirmed',
              sourceUrl: 'https://www.rockstargames.com/VI',
              sourceName: 'Rockstar Games',
            },
            {
              fact: 'Lucia is the series\u2019 first non-optional female protagonist',
              status: 'reported',
              sourceUrl: 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Theft_Auto_VI',
              sourceName: 'Wikipedia — Grand Theft Auto VI',
            },
            {
              fact: 'Lucia was imprisoned at Leonida Penitentiary after fighting for her family from Liberty City',
              status: 'reported',
              sourceUrl: 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Theft_Auto_VI',
              sourceName: 'Wikipedia — Grand Theft Auto VI',
            },
            {
              fact: 'Jason worked for local drug runners in the Leonida Keys after serving in the Army',
              status: 'reported',
              sourceUrl: 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Theft_Auto_VI',
              sourceName: 'Wikipedia — Grand Theft Auto VI',
            },
            {
              fact: 'The two protagonists are switchable during play',
              status: 'reported',
              sourceUrl: 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Theft_Auto_VI',
              sourceName: 'Wikipedia — Grand Theft Auto VI',
            },
            {
              fact: 'Rockstar has published the charges against Lucia or a detailed backstory for either character',
              status: 'unconfirmed',
            },
          ]}
        />

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          Two protagonists, one story
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          GTA 6 is built around a pair. Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos are the two protagonists
          of the single-player campaign, and the game follows their relationship — a duo
          inspired by Bonnie and Clyde, according to the documented coverage of the game. That
          is a deliberate break from GTA V, which had three protagonists who mostly operated
          independently, and from every earlier Grand Theft Auto, which had one. Here the
          story is the two of them together: a couple who want a normal life, who keep getting
          pulled back into crime, and whose choices drive the plot.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          The documented coverage says the two are switchable during play, in the style of GTA
          V&rsquo;s character switching. Rockstar has not published a detailed description of how
          switching works in GTA 6 — whether it is free at any time, whether missions lock you
          to one character, or how the two characters&rsquo; skills differ — so the mechanics are
          reported, not confirmed, and this page does not invent them. What is confirmed is
          simpler: there are two leads, both playable, and the story belongs to both of them.
          The game is a single-player campaign at launch, and no online mode has been announced.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          Lucia Caminos
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          Lucia is the most significant new character in the series&rsquo; history. She is the
          first non-optional female protagonist in a mainline Grand Theft Auto game — earlier
          games had women you could play in multiplayer or in side content, but never a woman
          leading the story. Trailer 1 opens on her, in prison, talking about coming home, and
          that image — Lucia in a cell, then Lucia walking out — is the first thing most
          players saw of GTA 6. She is not a sidekick to Jason&rsquo;s story. The trailers give
          her equal weight, and the story is hers as much as his.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          The documented background is that Lucia was imprisoned at Leonida Penitentiary after
          fighting for her family from Liberty City. That sentence is the full extent of what
          is documented about her past. Rockstar has not said what she was charged with, what
          crime she committed, how long she served, or what happened to her family — and this
          page will not fill those gaps with invented detail. The story, as far as it is
          officially known, starts with her release. She comes home to Vice City, reunites
          with Jason, and the two of them try to build a life together. The crime that follows
          is not a choice she makes lightly, and the trailers show her wrestling with it.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          Jason Duval
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          Jason is the other half of the duo, and the trailers present him as the quieter of
          the two. The documented background is that he worked for local drug runners in the
          Leonida Keys after serving in the Army — a past that explains both his skills and
          his reluctance to use them. Trailer 2 spends the most time with him: fixing roofs,
          working odd jobs, living a small, honest life in the Keys, and clearly trying to stay
          out of the business that once employed him. He is not a criminal mastermind and not
          an innocent bystander. He is a man with a past, trying to outrun it, who gets pulled
          back in by the person he loves.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          The dynamic between the two is the story&rsquo;s engine. Jason wants stability; Lucia
          wants a fresh start; neither of them gets one. After a failed bank heist, the duo
          encounters a conspiracy that spans the state of Leonida — that is the documented
          outline of the plot, and it is where the official summary stops. Everything beyond
          it — the twists, the betrayals, the ending — is unreleased, and any page that claims
          to know it is guessing. The honest version of the story is short: two people, a
          failed heist, a state-wide conspiracy, and a relationship under pressure.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          The supporting cast
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          Seven supporting characters are named in official material: <strong className="text-white">Cal Hampton</strong>,{' '}
          <strong className="text-white">Boobie Ike</strong>,{' '}
          <strong className="text-white">Dre&rsquo;Quan Priest</strong>,{' '}
          <strong className="text-white">Bae-Luxe</strong> and{' '}
          <strong className="text-white">Roxy</strong> — the duo known as Real Dimez —{' '}
          <strong className="text-white">Raul Bautista</strong>, and{' '}
          <strong className="text-white">Brian Heder</strong>. They appear in the trailers and on
          the official site&rsquo;s character material, and their names are documented. What has
          not been published is a detailed account of who each of them is, what they do, or how
          they connect to Jason and Lucia. The trailers give glimpses — Cal as Jason&rsquo;s friend
          and confidant, Boobie Ike as a local figure, Real Dimez as a music duo — but a
          glimpse is not a biography, and this page does not turn glimpses into backstories.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          That restraint matters, because character backstories are exactly the kind of detail
          that gets invented and then repeated as fact. A fan wiki can give Cal Hampton a full
          life story in a paragraph; a YouTube video can explain Raul Bautista&rsquo;s motives in
          ten minutes. None of it is official. Until the game launches on November 19, 2026,
          the supporting cast is a list of names and a handful of trailer moments. After
          launch, this page will be updated with what the game itself reveals — and the
          &ldquo;reported&rdquo; labels here will be resolved one by one.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          What to watch before launch
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          If you want to know Jason and Lucia before you play, the four official videos are
          the only reliable source. Trailer 1 (December 4, 2023) introduces Lucia. Trailer 2
          (May 6, 2025) introduces Jason and shows the two of them together. An Extended Look
          (August 27, 2026) shows them in action across Leonida for twenty-six minutes. The
          Launch Trailer (October 15, 2026) is the final ninety seconds. All four are on our{' '}
          <Link to="/gta-6-trailers" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">GTA 6 trailers page</Link>, embedded
          from the official Rockstar Games YouTube channel, with upload dates and durations
          verified. Anything else — a &ldquo;leaked&rdquo; character list, a supposed voice-actor
          reveal, a plot summary from an anonymous post — is not a source, and it is not
          repeated on this site. See our{' '}
          <Link to="/gta-6-leaks-vs-confirmed" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">leaks vs confirmed</Link> page
          for how we draw that line.
        </p>

        <FAQSection items={faq} title="Jason & Lucia — Questions" subtitle="" badge="" badgeColor="#FFC857" />

        <SourcesBox
          sources={[
            { name: 'Rockstar Games — official GTA VI page', url: 'https://www.rockstargames.com/VI' },
            { name: 'Wikipedia — Grand Theft Auto VI (Setting and characters)', url: 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Theft_Auto_VI' },

Those filings are real, but attributing the whole amount to GTA 6 is the author\u2019s inference, not a fact. Rockstar has denied reports that the game cost over $1.5 billion, without disclosing a specific figure.',

      answer: 'Grand Theft Auto V is widely cited at around $265 million in combined development and marketing spend when it launched in 2013 — then one of the most expensive games ever made. That figure is itself a reported estimate, not an official Rockstar number, but it is the standard comparison point for GTA 6\u2019s reported budget.',
    },
    {
      question: 'How much did Red Dead Redemption 2 cost?',
      answer: 'Rockstar has never published an official budget for Red Dead Redemption 2 either. The documented coverage of GTA 6\u2019s development notes that Rockstar\u2019s teams grew from 2,441 employees at RDR2\u2019s release to 4,711 across 12 offices during GTA 6\u2019s development — a much larger team, working longer, which is one reason the reported budget is so high.',
    },
    {
      question: 'Will Rockstar ever reveal the real budget?',
      answer: 'Probably not. Rockstar has never published a development budget for any Grand Theft Auto game, and Take-Two reports its finances in aggregate, not per game. The $1–1.5 billion analyst estimate is likely to remain the best available figure, and this page will keep labelling it as an estimate.',

  return (

        title="How Much Did GTA 6 Cost to Make?"
        description={description}
        canonical="/gta-6-development-cost"

        <div className="mt-6">

          <h1 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-black text-3xl sm:text-4xl text-white leading-tight">
            How Much Did GTA 6 Cost to Make?
          </h1>
          <p className="text-xs font-mono text-[#B9A6D4] mt-3">Last updated: November 5, 2026</p>
        </div>

        <QuickAnswer>
          Rockstar and Take-Two have published no official budget for GTA 6. The most widely
          cited estimate is $1 billion to $1.5 billion, from industry analysts cited by
          Business Insider in August 2026. Take-Two&rsquo;s CEO did not dispute the scale. Every
          figure on this page is a reported estimate — none of them is confirmed.
        </QuickAnswer>

        <FactsTable
          rows={[
            {
              fact: 'Rockstar / Take-Two have published an official GTA 6 development budget',
              status: 'unconfirmed',
            },
            {

            {

              sourceUrl: 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Theft_Auto_VI',
              sourceName: 'Wikipedia — Grand Theft Auto VI',
            },
            {
              fact: 'GTA V is widely cited at ~$265 million in combined development and marketing spend (2013)',
              status: 'reported',
              sourceUrl: 'https://gamesreviews.com/news/08/gta-6s-1-5-billion-budget-now-dwarfs-hollywoods-priciest-blockbusters-combined/',
              sourceName: 'GameReviews (Aug 30, 2026)',
            },
            {
              fact: 'Rockstar teams grew from 2,441 employees (RDR2 release) to 4,711 across 12 offices during GTA 6 development',
              status: 'reported',
              sourceUrl: 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Theft_Auto_VI',
              sourceName: 'Wikipedia — Grand Theft Auto VI',
            },
            {
              fact: 'GTA 6 cost $2 billion or more',
              status: 'unconfirmed',
            },
          ]}
        />

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          The reported estimate: $1–1.5 billion
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          The figure you will see most often is <strong className="text-white">$1 billion to
          $1.5 billion</strong>. It comes from industry analysts cited by Business Insider in
          August 2026, and it was reported by Engadget on August 29, 2026, in a piece comparing
          GTA 6&rsquo;s budget with the largest video-game budgets ever reported. The range is
          wide — half a billion dollars wide — because it is an estimate built from outside
          the company, not a number Rockstar has shared. Analysts arrive at it by looking at
          the size of the team, the length of the development, and the scale of the game, and
          then pricing those inputs. It is the best available figure, and it is still a guess.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          The most interesting thing anyone in authority has said about the budget is what
          Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick did not say. Asked about the reported figures, he did
          not dispute them. He said only that the game &ldquo;was expensive&rdquo; — a
          non-denial that has been read, reasonably, as confirmation that the scale is roughly
          right. It is not confirmation of a number. Zelnick has never given a figure, and
          Take-Two&rsquo;s financial reporting does not break out development costs per game.
          The $1–1.5 billion range is therefore the figure this site uses, always with the
          word &ldquo;reported&rdquo; attached, and always with the date it was reported.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          What Rockstar has denied — and what it hasn&rsquo;t
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          Rockstar has denied reports that GTA 6 cost over $1.5 billion, without disclosing a
          specific figure of its own. That denial is worth noting, because it puts a ceiling
          on the credible range: the $1–1.5 billion estimate sits inside it, and the larger
          figures sit outside it. It also shows the company&rsquo;s pattern — it will correct a
          number it considers wrong, but it will not supply a right one. The same pattern
          applies to the game itself: Rockstar corrects misinformation about release dates and
          prices, but it does not publish budgets, story lengths, or map sizes.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          The $2 billion figure deserves a paragraph of its own, because it circulates widely
          and sounds sourced. It traces to a social-media analysis of public filings for one
          Rockstar studio — Rockstar North, reported as Rockstar Games UK Ltd — showing about
          &pound;1.6 billion (roughly $2.1 billion) in wages from 2019 to 2025. Those filings
          are real, and the arithmetic is real. What is not real is the attribution: the wages
          are for one studio over six years, during which that studio worked on more than GTA
          6, and attributing the whole amount to one game is the author&rsquo;s inference, not
          a fact in the filings. This page omits the $2 billion figure from its facts table
          for exactly that reason — it cannot be sourced as a GTA 6 budget — and the denial
          above suggests it is too high in any case.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          How it compares: GTA 5, Red Dead Redemption 2, and Hollywood
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          The comparison that puts the estimate in perspective is GTA V. When it launched in
          2013, GTA V was widely cited at around <strong className="text-white">$265 million</strong> in
          combined development and marketing spend — then one of the most expensive games ever
          made. That figure is itself a reported estimate, not an official Rockstar number, but
          it is the standard comparison point, and the gap is the story: even at the low end of
          the GTA 6 estimate, the new game costs roughly four times what GTA V did, and at the
          high end, nearly six times. Part of that is inflation and part of it is scale — a
          bigger team, a longer development, and a whole state instead of a city.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          The Hollywood comparison is even starker. Engadget&rsquo;s August 2026 report noted
          that GTA 6&rsquo;s reported budget dwarfs the most expensive films ever made — and
          the court-document budgets it cited for other games show the gap inside the industry
          too: Horizon Forbidden West at $212 million, The Last of Us Part II at $220 million,
          and Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War at $700 million and above. GTA 6&rsquo;s
          reported $1–1.5 billion is more than double the largest of those. It is also worth
          remembering that development cost is not the whole cost: marketing, distribution,
          and the post-launch operation are separate, and Take-Two has not disclosed figures
          for those either.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          Why it cost so much
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          The documented coverage gives three reasons, and all three are consistent with the
          reported budget. The first is time: early work on GTA 6 began after Red Dead
          Redemption 2 in 2018, principal production started in 2020, and the game launches in
          November 2026 — roughly six years of full production, plus two years of early work,
          with two delays in between. The second is people: Rockstar&rsquo;s teams grew from
          2,441 employees at RDR2&rsquo;s release to 4,711 across 12 offices during GTA 6&rsquo;s
          development, nearly doubling. The third is scope: a whole state, two protagonists,
          and a level of detail that the trailers and An Extended Look make visible — a world
          that has to feel alive at street level and from the air. Long development, a large
          team, and a large world are the three most expensive things in game development, and
          GTA 6 has all three at maximum.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          None of that makes the $1–1.5 billion figure confirmed. It makes it plausible, and
          plausibility is not confirmation. The honest position for a site like this one is to
          use the reported estimate, date it, source it, and say plainly that the official
          figure does not exist. If Rockstar or Take-Two ever publishes a real budget, this
          page will be updated the same day — and the &ldquo;reported&rdquo; labels will become
          &ldquo;confirmed&rdquo;. Until then, the answer to &ldquo;how much did GTA 6 cost to
          make?&rdquo; is: somewhere between one and one and a half billion dollars, according
          to analysts, and nobody outside Rockstar knows for sure.
        </p>

        <FAQSection items={faq} title="Development cost — Questions" subtitle="" badge="" badgeColor="#FFC857" />

        <SourcesBox
          sources={[
            { name: 'Engadget — "The wildest video game budgets can\u2019t hold a candle to GTA 6" (Aug 29, 2026)', url: 'https://www.engadget.com/2246918/video-games-rival-gta-6-budget/' },
            { name: 'GameReviews — "GTA 6\u2019s $1.5 Billion Budget Now Dwarfs Hollywood\u2019s Priciest Blockbusters Combined" (Aug 30, 2026)', url: 'https://gamesreviews.com/news/08/gta-6s-1-5-billion-budget-now-dwarfs-hollywoods-priciest-blockbusters-combined/' },
            { name: 'Wikipedia — Grand Theft Auto VI (Development)', url: 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Theft_Auto_VI' },
          ]}
          lastVerified="2026-11-05"
        />

        <AuthorBox />

        <RelatedPages
          pages={[
            { name: 'GTA 6 trailers', path: '/gta-6-trailers' },
            { name: 'Story and length', path: '/gta-6-story-and-length' },
            { name: 'GTA 6 vs GTA 5', path: '/compare/gta-6-vs-gta-5' },
            { name: 'GTA 6 price', path: '/gta-6-price' },
            { name: 'GTA 6 editions', path: '/gta-6-editions' },
            { name: 'Leaks vs confirmed', path: '/gta-6-leaks-vs-confirmed' },
          ]}
        />
      </div>
    </>
  );
}

## src/pages/world/LeaksVsConfirmedPage.tsx

````tsx
import { Link } from 'react-router-dom';
import { ShieldCheck } from 'lucide-react';
import { SEO } from '../../components/SEO';
import { Breadcrumbs } from '../../components/Breadcrumbs';
import { QuickAnswer, FactsTable, SourcesBox, AuthorBox, RelatedPages } from '../../components/Article';
import { FAQSection } from '../../components/FAQSection';
import { articleSchema } from '../../lib/schema';
import { getAuthorName, SITE_CONFIG } from '../../config/site';

/**
 * Hub 3 spoke — leaks vs confirmed (policy page). This page contains NO
 * leaked material, NO links to leaks, and NO descriptions of leaked
 * content. It explains the confirmed / reported / rumor labels, the
 * site's no-leaks policy, and how to spot fake "free download" and
 * giveaway scams. Any claim about what leaked is deliberately absent.
 */
export function LeaksVsConfirmedPage() {
  const description =
    'What is confirmed about GTA 6, what is only reported, and what is a rumor or a scam. How we decide — and how to spot fake free-download offers.';
  const url = `${SITE_CONFIG.url}/gta-6-leaks-vs-confirmed`;

  const faq = [
    {
      question: 'Are the GTA 6 leaks real?',
      answer: 'Some material that appeared online before its official release was genuine — Rockstar itself acknowledged that early footage circulated before Trailer 1, and released the trailer early as a result. But "real" is not the same as "worth trusting": leaked material is incomplete, out of date, and shown without context, and this site does not publish it, link to it, or describe it. If a claim matters, wait for the official source.',
    },
    {
      question: 'Why doesn\u2019t VICE TOOLS publish leaks?',
      answer: 'Three reasons. First, leaks are unreliable — early footage and documents are outdated by the time they circulate, and they mislead more than they inform. Second, they are unfair to the people making the game, whose unfinished work is shown without their consent. Third, they are a security risk for readers: most "leak" links are malware, phishing, or scams. Our policy is to cover what is confirmed, label what is reported, and ignore the rest.',
    },
    {
      question: 'Is there a free GTA 6 download?',
      answer: 'No. There is no free GTA 6 download, no free beta, and no free early access. GTA 6 is a paid game — $79.99 for the Standard Edition, $99.99 for the Ultimate Edition — and the only legitimate way to get it is to pre-order or buy it from the PlayStation Store, the Xbox Store, or an authorised retailer. Any site, video, or message offering a free download is a scam.',
    },
    {
      question: 'Are GTA 6 giveaways real?',
      answer: 'Almost never. Giveaway posts promising a free copy of GTA 6 — usually asking you to click a link, enter your account details, or download a file — are scams. Rockstar has not announced any GTA 6 giveaway. A legitimate giveaway would be announced on rockstargames.com or the Rockstar Newswire, and it would never ask for your password or ask you to install software.',
    },
    {
      question: 'How do I tell a real GTA 6 claim from a fake one?',
      answer: 'Ask three questions. Does it come from rockstargames.com, the Rockstar Newswire, the PlayStation Store, or the Xbox Store? If not, is it from a named, reputable outlet that links to its own source? And does the claim appear on more than one independent source? If the answer to all three is no — and especially if it asks you to download something or enter credentials — treat it as a rumor or a scam.',
    },
    {
      question: 'What does "reported" mean on this site?',
      answer: 'Reported means a claim comes from a named source — a reputable outlet, a court document, or documented reference coverage — but has not been confirmed by Rockstar, Take-Two, PlayStation, or Xbox. Reported claims are labelled as reported, dated, and sourced on every page. "Confirmed" is reserved for official sources only. Anything with no source at all is a rumor, and rumors are not published here.',
    },
  ];

  return (
    <>
      <SEO
        title="GTA 6 Leaks vs Confirmed Facts"
        description={description}
        canonical="/gta-6-leaks-vs-confirmed"
        type="article"
        articlePublished="2026-11-05"
        articleModified="2026-11-05"
        ogImage="https://vicetools.app/og-map.png"
        schema={articleSchema({
          headline: 'GTA 6 Leaks vs Confirmed Facts',
          description,
          datePublished: '2026-11-05',
          dateModified: '2026-11-05',
          authorName: getAuthorName(),
          url,
        })}
      />

      <div className="max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8 py-10">
        <Breadcrumbs pathname="/gta-6-leaks-vs-confirmed" />

        <div className="mt-6">
          <div className="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-3 py-1 rounded-full bg-[#150A24] border border-[#19E3D0]/40 text-xs font-mono text-[#19E3D0] mb-3">
            <ShieldCheck className="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
            <span>WE DO NOT PUBLISH LEAKS</span>
          </div>
          <h1 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-black text-3xl sm:text-4xl text-white leading-tight">
            Leaks vs Confirmed
          </h1>
          <p className="text-xs font-mono text-[#B9A6D4] mt-3">Last updated: November 5, 2026</p>
        </div>

        <QuickAnswer>
          This page explains how VICE TOOLS decides what is true about GTA 6 — and what it
          refuses to publish. Confirmed means an official source said it. Reported means a
          named, reputable source said it but Rockstar has not confirmed it. Everything else
          is a rumor, and rumors are not published here. Leaks are never published, linked, or
          described.
        </QuickAnswer>

        <FactsTable
          rows={[
            {
              fact: 'GTA 6 launches November 19, 2026, on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S',
              status: 'confirmed',
              sourceUrl: 'https://www.rockstargames.com/newswire/article/ak3ak31a49a221/grand-theft-auto-vi-is-now-set-to-launch-november-19-2026',

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          The three labels
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          Every fact on this site carries one of three labels, and the labels are the whole
          point of the site. <strong className="text-white">Confirmed</strong> means the claim
          comes from an official source: Rockstar Games Newswire, rockstargames.com/VI, the
          PlayStation Store, or the Xbox Store. A confirmed claim has a source URL and a
          last-verified date, and the build fails if either is missing. The release date,
          the prices, the editions, the pre-load date, and the 212 GB file size are all
          confirmed in that sense — you can click through to the official source and check
          them yourself.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          <strong className="text-white">Reported</strong> means the claim comes from a named,
          reputable source — a known outlet, a court document, or documented reference coverage
          — but Rockstar, Take-Two, PlayStation, or Xbox has not confirmed it. The $1–1.5
          billion development-cost estimate is reported. The 80-hour playthrough is reported.
          The claim that the map is three times larger than Red Dead Redemption 2&rsquo;s is
          reported. Reported claims are always labelled as reported, always dated, and always
          sourced to the outlet that made them, so you can judge the source for yourself.{' '}
          <strong className="text-white">Rumor</strong> means a claim with no source at all — a
          social-media post, an anonymous forum thread, a video with no citation. Rumors are
          not published on this site, even to debunk them, because repeating a rumor gives it
          reach it has not earned.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          Why we do not publish leaks
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          GTA 6 has had leaks. Material appeared online before its official release, and
          Rockstar itself acknowledged that early footage circulated before Trailer 1 — and
          released the trailer early as a result. This page does not describe that material, does
          not link to it, and does not summarise what it showed. That is a policy, not an
          oversight, and it has three reasons.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          First, leaks are unreliable. Early footage and documents are outdated by the time
          they circulate — they show a game months or years from release, missing features,
          placeholder content, and systems that have since changed. A reader who trusts a leak
          learns the wrong game. Second, leaks are unfair to the people making the game, whose
          unfinished work is shown without their consent, often in a form they would never
          choose to share. Third, and most practically, leaks are a security risk for readers:
          most links promising leaked footage are malware, phishing pages, or scams, and the
          safest advice about them is not to click. The same rule applies to our{' '}
          <Link to="/gta-6-trailers" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">trailers page</Link>: only
          the four official videos, embedded from the official Rockstar Games YouTube channel,
          and nothing else.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          How to spot a fake
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          The most common GTA 6 scam is the &ldquo;free download&rdquo;. There is no free GTA 6
          download, no free beta, and no free early access. GTA 6 is a paid game — $79.99 for
          the Standard Edition, $99.99 for the Ultimate Edition — and the only legitimate way
          to get it is to pre-order or buy it from the PlayStation Store, the Xbox Store, or an
          authorised retailer. Any site, video, message, or social-media post offering a free
          download is a scam, and the file it offers is almost certainly malware. The same
          applies to &ldquo;free GTA 6&rdquo; giveaways: Rockstar has not announced any GTA 6
          giveaway, and a legitimate giveaway would be announced on rockstargames.com or the
          Rockstar Newswire — and would never ask for your password or ask you to install
          software. See our{' '}
          <Link to="/gta-6-download" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">download page</Link> for
          the legitimate routes, and nothing else.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          For claims rather than downloads, the test is simple. Ask three questions. Does it
          come from rockstargames.com, the Rockstar Newswire, the PlayStation Store, or the
          Xbox Store? If not, is it from a named, reputable outlet that links to its own
          source? And does the claim appear on more than one independent source? If the answer
          to all three is no — and especially if the claim asks you to download something, enter
          credentials, or pay for &ldquo;early access&rdquo; — treat it as a rumor or a scam.
          A claim that fails all three tests has not earned your trust, however many times it
          has been reposted. If you are ever unsure about a specific claim, the{' '}
          <Link to="/gta-6-faq" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">FAQ hub</Link> answers the
          thirty most-asked questions with their sources, and the{' '}
          <Link to="/about/methodology" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">methodology page</Link> explains
          how this site verifies every fact it publishes.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          What changes after launch
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          On November 19, 2026, the labels on this site start resolving. Claims that were
          reported — the map size, the story length, the supporting cast — will be confirmed or
          corrected against the game itself, and this page will be updated with the results.
          The no-leaks policy does not change after launch: the game itself is the source, and
          there is nothing left to leak. What does change is the volume of real information,
          and the site&rsquo;s job shifts from saying what is not yet known to documenting what
          is. The methodology page carries the update log for that process, and the{' '}
          <Link to="/data/facts.json" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">facts file</Link> —
          the machine-readable list of every sourced claim on this site — is updated with it.
        </p>

        <FAQSection items={faq} title="Leaks vs confirmed — Questions" subtitle="" badge="" badgeColor="#FFC857" />

        <SourcesBox
          sources={[
            { name: 'Rockstar Games Newswire — launch date', url: 'https://www.rockstargames.com/newswire/article/ak3ak31a49a221/grand-theft-auto-vi-is-now-set-to-launch-november-19-2026' },
            { name: 'Rockstar Games — official GTA VI page', url: 'https://www.rockstargames.com/VI' },
            { name: 'Rockstar Games — Editions', url: 'https://www.rockstargames.com/VI/editions' },
            { name: 'VICE TOOLS — Methodology', url: 'https://vicetools.app/about/methodology' },
          ]}
          lastVerified="2026-11-05"
        />

        <AuthorBox />

        <RelatedPages

            { name: 'Development cost', path: '/gta-6-development-cost' },
            { name: 'GTA 6 release date', path: '/gta-6-release-date' },
          ]}
        />
      </div>
    </>
  );
}

        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">

            {

              status: 'unconfirmed',
