````tsx
            {
              fact: 'The 80-hour figure is a player average or an official length',
              status: 'unconfirmed',
            },
          ]}
        />

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          The honest answer: nobody knows yet
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          Every &ldquo;how long to beat GTA 6&rdquo; article you will find before launch is
          guessing. Rockstar has not published a story length, a main-story hour count, or a
          completionist figure for GTA 6, and it has never done so for a Grand Theft Auto game
          before launch. The studio does not talk about its games in hours. What it talks
          about is the story — Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, a failed bank heist, a conspiracy
          across the state of Leonida — and the world they move through. How long that story
          takes to play is something players discover, not something Rockstar announces.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          That does not mean there is nothing to say. There is one concrete number, one set of
          comparisons, and a clear picture of why the game is likely to be long. This page
          gives you all three, with each one labelled for what it is: a reported single run,
          player averages for other games, and an estimate — never a confirmed GTA 6 length.
          If you came here for a single number, the closest thing to one is eighty hours, and
          the next section explains why even that number needs a paragraph of qualification.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          The 80-hour run
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          In August 2026, Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson told The New York Times
          that his own GTA 6 playthrough — main story plus some optional objectives, finished
          in February 2026 — took about 80 hours. That is the only first-hand completion time
          that has ever been attached to the game, and it is worth taking seriously, because it
          comes from the person running the studio that made it. It is also worth taking
          carefully, because of what it is not. It is not a player average. It is not a
          main-story-only time. It is not a completionist time. It is one person, playing one
          way, on a build of the game from February 2026 — nine months before launch, when the
          game was still being polished.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          Read it as a lower bound on the game&rsquo;s scale rather than a prediction of your
          own playtime. A studio head playing his own game knows where everything is, skips
          nothing important, and still needed eighty hours for the story plus some side
          content. A first-time player, exploring Leonida, failing missions, and stopping to
          look around, will almost certainly take longer for the same content. And a player
          who rushes the main story, skipping side activities, will take less. The eighty hours
          tells you the game is long. It does not tell you how long it will take you.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          How GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 compare
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          The best reference points are Rockstar&rsquo;s two most recent open-world games, and
          their numbers come from HowLongToBeat player averages, checked on October 21, 2026.
          Grand Theft Auto V averages <strong className="text-white">32 hours</strong> for the
          main story, <strong className="text-white">51.5 hours</strong> for the main story
          plus extras, and <strong className="text-white">89.5 hours</strong> for completionists.
          Red Dead Redemption 2 averages <strong className="text-white">51 hours</strong> for
          the main story, <strong className="text-white">84.5 hours</strong> for the main story
          plus extras, and <strong className="text-white">196 hours</strong> for completionists.
          Those are real numbers, from thousands of players — but they are numbers for GTA V
          and RDR2, not for GTA 6, and this page does not present them as GTA 6&rsquo;s length.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          They are useful in two ways. First, they set a floor: GTA 6 is built by a larger
          team than either game, in a world that is a whole state rather than a city, and its
          one reported run already sits above GTA V&rsquo;s main-story average. Second, they
          show how much the answer depends on how you play — the gap between &ldquo;main
          story&rdquo; and &ldquo;completionist&rdquo; is nearly three times for GTA V and nearly
          four times for RDR2. Whatever GTA 6&rsquo;s numbers turn out to be, the spread will be
          just as wide. A &ldquo;how long&rdquo; answer that gives you one number without saying
          which kind of playthrough it describes is not an answer. See our{' '}
          <Link to="/compare/gta-6-vs-gta-5" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">GTA 6 vs GTA 5</Link> and{' '}
          <Link to="/compare/gta-6-vs-red-dead-redemption-2" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">GTA 6 vs Red Dead Redemption 2</Link> pages
          for the full comparisons.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          What makes GTA 6 long — and what could make it longer
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          Three things point to a long game, and all three are estimates, not measurements.
          The first is the world: a whole state, with a city, the Keys, wetlands, a national
          park, and a port, is more ground to cover than any previous Grand Theft Auto, and
          travel time is playtime. The second is the story: two protagonists, a conspiracy
          across the state, and a supporting cast of seven named characters suggest a plot with
          more threads than GTA V&rsquo;s three-character structure. The third is the team: the
          documented coverage notes that Rockstar&rsquo;s teams grew from 2,441 employees at
          Red Dead Redemption 2&rsquo;s release to 4,711 across 12 offices during GTA 6&rsquo;s
          development — a much larger team, working longer, on a bigger world.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          None of that converts into hours. A bigger world can mean longer travel or faster
          travel, depending on the design. A bigger team can mean more content or more polish
          on the same content. And the eighty-hour run, for all its authority, is a single
          data point from a build that is now months old. The responsible way to think about
          GTA 6&rsquo;s length before launch is as a range with a floor: the story plus some side
          content took a senior developer eighty hours, and most players will take longer than
          that for the same content. The ceiling — completionist time, all activities, all
          collectibles — is unknowable until the game is out, because nobody outside Rockstar
          knows what &ldquo;all&rdquo; even includes yet.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          When we will know
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          The real numbers arrive fast after launch. GTA 6 unlocks at local midnight on
          November 19, 2026, and the first players will finish the main story within days.
          Reviewers will publish their completion times, HowLongToBeat will start collecting
          player averages, and the &ldquo;how long&rdquo; question will get real answers — main
          story, main plus extras, and completionist, each with a sample size behind it. This
          page will be updated with those figures, sourced and dated, as soon as they exist.
          Until then, the honest answer stays the same: no official length, one reported
          eighty-hour run, and two older games as reference points. If you want the practical
          side of launch — when the game unlocks in your country and how to pre-load it — the{' '}
          <Link to="/gta-6-release-time" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">release-time hub</Link> and{' '}
          <Link to="/gta-6-preload" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">pre-load page</Link> have the
          confirmed times.
        </p>

        <FAQSection items={faq} title="Story length — Questions" subtitle="" badge="" badgeColor="#FFC857" />

        <SourcesBox
          sources={[
````

````tsx
        <h3 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-lg text-white mt-8 mb-2">
          Trailer 1 — December 4, 2023
        </h3>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-3 font-light">
          Ninety seconds that broke the internet. Trailer 1 introduces Lucia — in prison, then
          walking out — and modern Vice City in the same breath: the beachfront, the neon
          streets, the skyline at dusk, and a city that looks like Miami and feels like a
          Rockstar game. It was published on December 4, 2023, after a leak forced Rockstar to
          release it early, and it remains the most-watched video game trailer ever published.
          Watch it for Lucia and for the city. Everything else in the game&rsquo;s marketing
          builds on these ninety seconds.
        </p>
        <div className="aspect-video w-full rounded-xl overflow-hidden border border-white/10 my-4">
          <iframe
            className="w-full h-full"
            src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/QdBZY2fkU-0"
            title="Grand Theft Auto VI Trailer 1"
            allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share"
            allowFullScreen
            loading="lazy"
          />
        </div>
        <p className="text-xs text-[#B9A6D4] my-2">
          Source:{' '}
          <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QdBZY2fkU-0" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">
            Rockstar Games YouTube — Grand Theft Auto VI Trailer 1
          </a>{' '}
          (December 4, 2023, 1 min 30 sec).
        </p>

        <h3 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-lg text-white mt-8 mb-2">
          Trailer 2 — May 6, 2025
        </h3>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-3 font-light">
          Two minutes and forty-seven seconds, and the first real look at Jason. Trailer 2
          opens in the Leonida Keys — Jason fixing roofs, working odd jobs, living a small life
          — and follows the two of them as Lucia&rsquo;s release pulls him back into crime. It
          is the trailer that shows the state, not just the city: the Keys, the highways, the
          small towns, and the countryside that makes Leonida a place rather than a backdrop.
          It is also the trailer that confirmed the second delay in the same announcement, moving
          the release from May 26, 2026 to November 19, 2026. Note: this upload is
          age-restricted on YouTube, so the embed may ask you to watch on YouTube while signed
          in.
        </p>
        <div className="aspect-video w-full rounded-xl overflow-hidden border border-white/10 my-4">
          <iframe
            className="w-full h-full"
            src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/VQRLujxTm3c"
            title="Grand Theft Auto VI Trailer 2"
            allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share"
            allowFullScreen
            loading="lazy"
          />
        </div>
        <p className="text-xs text-[#B9A6D4] my-2">
          Source:{' '}
          <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VQRLujxTm3c" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">
            Rockstar Games YouTube — Grand Theft Auto VI Trailer 2
          </a>{' '}
          (May 6, 2025, 2 min 47 sec, age-restricted).
        </p>

        <h3 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-lg text-white mt-8 mb-2">
          An Extended Look — August 27, 2026
        </h3>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-3 font-light">
          The most useful video Rockstar has ever released for a Grand Theft Auto game.
          Twenty-six minutes and forty-eight seconds of in-game footage, captured entirely on
          PlayStation 5, showing chases, robberies, and activities across different parts of
          Leonida — city streets, the Keys, wetlands, and rural roads. It premiered on
          Netflix at 3:00 PM ET on August 27, 2026, then went free on YouTube and
          rockstargames.com/VI at 9:00 PM ET the same day. If you want to know what the game
          actually looks like to play, this is the video. Like Trailer 2, it is age-restricted
          on YouTube, so the embed may ask you to watch on YouTube while signed in.
        </p>
        <div className="aspect-video w-full rounded-xl overflow-hidden border border-white/10 my-4">
          <iframe
            className="w-full h-full"
            src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/tJbzMqJGH4k"
            title="Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look"
            allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share"
            allowFullScreen
            loading="lazy"
          />
        </div>
        <p className="text-xs text-[#B9A6D4] my-2">
          Source:{' '}
          <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tJbzMqJGH4k" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">
            Rockstar Games YouTube — Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look
          </a>{' '}
          (August 27, 2026, 26 min 48 sec, age-restricted).
        </p>

        <h3 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-lg text-white mt-8 mb-2">
          Launch Trailer — October 15, 2026
        </h3>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-3 font-light">
          Ninety seconds, published on October 15, 2026, on the Rockstar Newswire and the
          Rockstar Games YouTube channel, with footage captured in-game on PlayStation 5. The
          Launch Trailer is the final official video before release: a last, polished look at
          Vice City, Jason and Lucia, and the world they are about to enter. It is not
          age-restricted, so it plays directly in the embed below. If you only watch one video
          on this page, watch this one — then watch An Extended Look for the full picture.
        </p>
        <div className="aspect-video w-full rounded-xl overflow-hidden border border-white/10 my-4">
          <iframe
            className="w-full h-full"
            src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/rz1B4B2yBZY"
            title="Grand Theft Auto VI Launch Trailer"
            allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share"
            allowFullScreen
            loading="lazy"
          />
        </div>
        <p className="text-xs text-[#B9A6D4] my-2">
          Source:{' '}
          <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rz1B4B2yBZY" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">
            Rockstar Games YouTube — Grand Theft Auto VI Launch Trailer
          </a>{' '}
          (October 15, 2026, 1 min 30 sec).
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          What the trailers show — and what they don&rsquo;t
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          Taken together, the four videos are the best public evidence of what GTA 6 is. They
          show the setting — Vice City and the state of Leonida — the two protagonists, the
          supporting cast, and the range of activities, from heists to quiet moments in the
          Keys. An Extended Look is the most informative, because twenty-six minutes of
          gameplay shows more than four trailers combined: the driving, the shooting, the
          world&rsquo;s density, and the way the game moves between city and countryside. What
          the videos do not show is equally important. No trailer includes a map screen, a
          fast-travel menu, a distance marker, or a mission list. No trailer shows the online
          mode, because no online mode has been announced. And no trailer gives a story length,
          a budget, or a PC release date — those questions are answered on their own pages,
          with the same discipline: confirmed where Rockstar has said it, reported where it
          has not.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          One more thing the trailers do not do is number themselves the way fans expect.
          Rockstar has never published a video titled &ldquo;Trailer 3&rdquo;. The sequence is
          Trailer 1, Trailer 2, An Extended Look, and the Launch Trailer — and the third video
          is called An Extended Look, not Trailer 3. Any video claiming to be &ldquo;GTA 6
          Trailer 3&rdquo; is either a fan edit or a mislabelled re-upload. The same applies to
          any video titled &ldquo;gameplay trailer&rdquo;: Rockstar has not released one, and
          An Extended Look is the closest official equivalent. If a video is not on this page
          and not on the Rockstar Games YouTube channel, it is not official.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          How this page will change
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          If Rockstar publishes another video before launch on November 19, 2026, it will be
          added here with its real upload date, real duration, and a VideoObject entry — the
          same standard applied to the four videos above. After launch, the page will also
          note any official post-launch videos, such as an online-mode reveal if one is
          announced. What will never appear here is leaked footage, a re-upload from an
          unofficial channel, or a fan edit presented as official. The rule for this page is
          the rule for the whole site: if it is not on rockstargames.com, the Rockstar Newswire,
          or the official Rockstar Games YouTube channel, it is not on VICE TOOLS. See our{' '}
          <Link to="/gta-6-leaks-vs-confirmed" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">leaks vs confirmed</Link> page
          for the full policy.
        </p>

        <FAQSection items={faq} title="Trailers — Questions" subtitle="" badge="" badgeColor="#FFC857" />

        <SourcesBox
          sources={[
            { name: 'Rockstar Games YouTube — Grand Theft Auto VI Trailer 1', url: 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QdBZY2fkU-0' },
            { name: 'Rockstar Games YouTube — Grand Theft Auto VI Trailer 2', url: 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VQRLujxTm3c' },
            { name: 'Rockstar Games YouTube — Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look', url: 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tJbzMqJGH4k' },
            { name: 'Rockstar Games YouTube — Grand Theft Auto VI Launch Trailer', url: 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rz1B4B2yBZY' },
````

## src/pages/world/ViceCityLeonidaPage.tsx

````tsx
import { Link } from 'react-router-dom';
import { MapPin } from 'lucide-react';
import { SEO } from '../../components/SEO';
import { Breadcrumbs } from '../../components/Breadcrumbs';
import { QuickAnswer, FactsTable, SourcesBox, AuthorBox, RelatedPages } from '../../components/Article';
import { FAQSection } from '../../components/FAQSection';
import { articleSchema } from '../../lib/schema';
import { getAuthorName, SITE_CONFIG } from '../../config/site';

/**
 * Hub 3 spoke — Vice City and Leonida. The basis is stated as widely
 * documented (Vice City ~ Miami, Leonida ~ Florida) and sourced; no
 * specific real-world analogue is invented beyond that. The 2002 game is
 * discussed only as series history, not as a fact about GTA 6.
 */
export function ViceCityLeonidaPage() {
  const description =
    "Vice City is GTA 6's Miami-inspired city in Leonida, Rockstar's fictional Florida. What the trailers show and what is still unconfirmed.";
  const url = `${SITE_CONFIG.url}/gta-6-vice-city-leonida`;

  const faq = [
    {
      question: 'What city is GTA 6 based on?',
      answer: 'GTA 6 is set in Vice City, Rockstar\u2019s fictional version of Miami, Florida, in the fictional state of Leonida (based on Florida). That is the widely documented basis for the setting, and it matches everything in the trailers — the beaches, the neon streets, the skyline, and the Keys.',
    },
    {
      question: 'Is GTA 6 set in the same Vice City as the 2002 game?',
      answer: 'It is the same fictional city, rebuilt for the modern era. GTA 6 returns to Vice City more than twenty years after the 2002 game, but the setting is contemporary — smartphones, social media, and a modern Miami look — not a period remake. The 2002 game is series history; GTA 6 is a new story in the same city.',
    },
    {
      question: 'How big is Leonida compared to Vice City?',
      answer: 'Leonida is the whole state; Vice City is its main city. The trailers show places far beyond the city — the Leonida Keys, the Grassrivers wetlands, highways, and small towns — so the game world is a state, not a city with countryside attached. Rockstar has not published a map or a size, so no square-mile figure is given here.',
    },
    {
      question: 'What places in Leonida have been named?',
      answer: 'Areas named in official material include Vice City, Grassrivers, and the Leonida Keys — inspired by Miami, the Everglades, and the Florida Keys — plus Ambrosia, Mount Kalaga National Park, and Port Gellhorn. Those names are reported, and their exact positions have not been published.',
    },
    {
      question: 'Is Leonida a real place?',
      answer: 'No. Leonida is fictional, just as Vice City is fictional. It is Rockstar\u2019s version of Florida — the name, the geography, and the culture are invented, even though the inspiration is obvious. The same applies to every place name in the game: inspired by real Florida, not a copy of it.',
    },
    {
      question: 'Will GTA 6 show other cities besides Vice City?',
      answer: 'Rockstar has not announced any other cities. The confirmed setting is Vice City and the wider state of Leonida, with the named areas above. Any claim about additional cities is speculation unless Rockstar says so.',
    },
  ];

  return (
    <>
      <SEO
        title="GTA 6 Vice City & Leonida Guide"
        description={description}
        canonical="/gta-6-vice-city-leonida"
        type="article"
        articlePublished="2026-11-05"
        articleModified="2026-11-05"
        ogImage="https://vicetools.app/og-map.png"
        schema={articleSchema({
          headline: 'GTA 6 Vice City & Leonida Guide',
          description,
          datePublished: '2026-11-05',
          dateModified: '2026-11-05',
          authorName: getAuthorName(),
          url,
        })}
      />

      <div className="max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8 py-10">
        <Breadcrumbs pathname="/gta-6-vice-city-leonida" />

        <div className="mt-6">
          <div className="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-3 py-1 rounded-full bg-[#150A24] border border-[#19E3D0]/40 text-xs font-mono text-[#19E3D0] mb-3">
            <MapPin className="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
            <span>VICE CITY • STATE OF LEONIDA</span>
          </div>
          <h1 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-black text-3xl sm:text-4xl text-white leading-tight">
            Vice City &amp; Leonida
          </h1>
          <p className="text-xs font-mono text-[#B9A6D4] mt-3">Last updated: November 5, 2026</p>
        </div>

        <QuickAnswer>
          GTA 6 is set in Vice City — Rockstar&rsquo;s fictional version of Miami — in the
          fictional state of Leonida, based on Florida. It is the same city the series first
          visited in 2002, rebuilt for the modern era, and this time the whole state around
          it is part of the game.
        </QuickAnswer>

        <FactsTable
          rows={[
            {
              fact: 'GTA 6 is set in Vice City, in the state of Leonida',
              status: 'confirmed',
              sourceUrl: 'https://www.rockstargames.com/VI',
              sourceName: 'Rockstar Games',
            },
            {
              fact: 'Vice City is a fictionalised version of Miami; Leonida is based on Florida',
              status: 'reported',
              sourceUrl: 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Theft_Auto_VI',
              sourceName: 'Wikipedia — Grand Theft Auto VI',
            },
            {
              fact: 'Leonida is a real place',
              status: 'unconfirmed',
            },
            {
              fact: 'Named areas: Vice City, Grassrivers, Leonida Keys, Ambrosia, Mount Kalaga National Park, Port Gellhorn',
              status: 'reported',
              sourceUrl: 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Theft_Auto_VI',
              sourceName: 'Wikipedia — Grand Theft Auto VI',
            },
            {
              fact: 'GTA 6 is a period remake of the 2002 game',
              status: 'unconfirmed',
            },
            {
              fact: 'Other cities beyond Vice City have been announced',
              status: 'unconfirmed',
            },
          ]}
        />

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          Vice City, again
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          Vice City is the most famous fictional city in video games, and GTA 6 is its
          homecoming. The city first appeared in 2002, in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, as a
          neon-soaked version of 1980s Miami — pastel hotels, palm trees, a beachfront strip,
          and a criminal underworld that felt like a movie. It became the series&rsquo; signature
          setting, the one players ask about more than any other, and for two decades Rockstar
          left it alone. GTA 6 brings it back, not as a remake and not as a period piece, but
          as a modern city: smartphones, social media, a contemporary skyline, and the same
          beaches and boulevards rebuilt for a game made in the 2020s.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          The basis is widely documented: Vice City is a fictionalised version of Miami,
          Florida. The trailers make the inspiration obvious — Ocean Drive-style beachfront
          hotels, a downtown skyline, the neon, the palm trees, the water everywhere. But
          &ldquo;based on Miami&rdquo; is not the same as &ldquo;a copy of Miami&rdquo;. Vice City is
          invented: its streets, its districts, and its landmarks are Rockstar&rsquo;s creations,
          arranged for gameplay rather than geography. Players who know Miami will recognise
          the feeling; they should not expect to navigate it with a real map.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          Leonida: the whole state
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          The bigger change in GTA 6 is not the city — it is everything around it. Leonida is
          the fictional state, based on Florida, and the game is set in the state, not just in
          Vice City. The trailers keep leaving the city: the Leonida Keys stretch out to sea,
          the Grassrivers wetlands spread inland, highways run past small towns, and the
          countryside is where a surprising amount of the action happens. That is a different
          structure from the 2002 game, which was a city with a couple of islands, and it is
          closer to the structure of Red Dead Redemption 2 — a large region with a city inside
          it, rather than a city with a region attached.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          The names that have been documented for Leonida&rsquo;s regions map neatly onto real
          Florida, and it is worth naming the inspirations once, plainly: Grassrivers is the
          Everglades, the Leonida Keys are the Florida Keys, and Vice City is Miami. The other
          documented names — Ambrosia, Mount Kalaga National Park, Port Gellhorn — have no
          obvious single real-world analogue, and no specific analogue is claimed here. What
          matters for players is the variety: a city, a coast, a wetland, a national park, and
          a port, all inside one state. That variety is what the trailers keep showing, and it
          is what makes Leonida feel like a place rather than a backdrop.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          What the trailers show
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          Trailer 1 (December 4, 2023) is almost entirely Vice City: the beachfront, the
          streets, the skyline at dusk, and Lucia&rsquo;s voice over the city she is coming home
          to. Trailer 2 (May 6, 2025) widens the lens — Jason in the Keys, the two of them on
          highways and in small towns, and a lot of time outside the city limits. An Extended
          Look (August 27, 2026) is the most geographically useful of the four: twenty-six
          minutes and forty-eight seconds of in-game footage, captured on PlayStation 5, that
          moves between city streets, the Keys, wetlands, and rural roads without ever cutting
          to a map. The Launch Trailer (October 15, 2026) returns to the city for its final
          ninety seconds. All four are embedded on our{' '}
          <Link to="/gta-6-trailers" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">GTA 6 trailers page</Link>, from the
          official Rockstar Games YouTube channel.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          Taken together, the videos show a world that is dense in the city and open outside
          it. The city scenes are crowded — traffic, pedestrians, neon, storefronts — and the
          countryside scenes are wide: water, flat land, long roads, and a horizon that keeps
          going. That contrast is the point of setting the game in a state. It also explains
          the install size: the pre-load file is up to 212 GB, and a world this varied, at this
          level of detail, is why. The size is confirmed; the map itself is not, and the two
          facts should not be confused.
        </p>

        <h2 className="font-['Orbitron'] font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl text-white mt-10 mb-4">
          What is still unknown
        </h2>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          For all the footage, several basic questions about the setting have no official
          answer. There is no official map, so no one can say where Ambrosia sits relative to
          Vice City, how far the Keys stretch, or where Mount Kalaga rises. There is no
          confirmed district list for Vice City itself — no official names for its
          neighbourhoods, no confirmed count of districts, and no statement about which parts
          of the 2002 map return. There is no confirmed answer to whether other cities exist
          in Leonida beyond the named areas, and no official size for the world. The one size
          figure in circulation — three times the playable area of Red Dead Redemption 2 — is
          a report, not a confirmation, and it is labelled that way on our{' '}
          <Link to="/gta-6-map" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">GTA 6 map page</Link>.
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-[#B9A6D4] leading-relaxed my-4 font-light">
          Those gaps will close on November 19, 2026, when the game launches and players can
          see the world for themselves. Until then, the honest guide to Vice City and Leonida
          is a short list: a confirmed setting, a documented basis in Miami and Florida, six
          named areas, four trailers, and a lot of unknown geography. That is what this page
          gives you. If you want the practical side — when the game unlocks in your country,
          and how to pre-load it — the{' '}
          <Link to="/gta-6-release-time" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">release-time hub</Link> and the{' '}
          <Link to="/gta-6-preload" className="text-[#19E3D0] underline hover:text-white">pre-load page</Link> have the
          confirmed times.
        </p>

        <FAQSection items={faq} title="Vice City & Leonida — Questions" subtitle="" badge="" badgeColor="#FFC857" />

        <SourcesBox
          sources={[
            { name: 'Rockstar Games — official GTA VI page', url: 'https://www.rockstargames.com/VI' },
            { name: 'Wikipedia — Grand Theft Auto VI (Setting and characters)', url: 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Theft_Auto_VI' },
            { name: 'Rockstar Games YouTube — Grand Theft Auto VI Trailer 2', url: 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VQRLujxTm3c' },
          ]}
          lastVerified="2026-11-05"
        />

        <RelatedPages

            { name: 'GTA 6 release date', path: '/gta-6-release-date' },
          ]}
        />
      </div>
    </>
  );
}
````

## vite.config.ts

````ts
import tailwindcss from '@tailwindcss/vite';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';

// ESM-safe __dirname equivalent (vite.config.ts is an ES module).
const rootDir = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));

export default defineConfig(({ isSsrBuild }) => {
  return {
    plugins: [react(), tailwindcss()],
    resolve: {
      alias: {
        '@': rootDir,
      },
    },
    server: {
      // HMR is disabled in AI Studio via DISABLE_HMR env var.
      // Do not modify—file watching is disabled to prevent flickering during agent edits.
      hmr: process.env.DISABLE_HMR !== 'true',
      // Disable file watching when DISABLE_HMR is true to save CPU during agent edits.
      watch: process.env.DISABLE_HMR === 'true' ? null : {},
    },
    build: {
      // Vite preloads dynamic-import chunks reachable from the entry by
      // injecting <link rel="modulepreload"> into index.html. That pulled
      // the 407 kB recharts chunk into <head> on EVERY prerendered page
      // (verified: all 69 built HTML files preloaded it), defeating the
      // manualChunks split. Keep preload for the runtime and route chunks,
      // but never for the heavy tool libraries — they load on demand when
      // their page mounts. Removing a preload hint can never break loading.
      modulePreload: {
        resolveDependencies: (_filename, deps) =>
          deps.filter((dep) => !dep.includes('leaflet') && !dep.includes('recharts')),
      },
      rollupOptions: {
        output: {
          // Split the heavy tool libraries out of the main bundle so they
          // load only on the pages that use them (Leaflet: /map, Recharts:
          // calculator charts). Disabled for the SSR build, which needs a
          // single server bundle for the prerender script.
          manualChunks: isSsrBuild
            ? undefined
            : (id: string) => {
                if (id.includes('node_modules/leaflet')) return 'leaflet';
                if (id.includes('node_modules/recharts')) return 'recharts';
                return undefined;
              },
        },
      },
    },
  };
});

````
